chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: Cootie Williams's hometown Mobile and watermelon
summary: The Mobile station was packed for Cootie, then the band played a segregated dance.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And man, I was sleeping. I heard all this noise, I raised the little shade and saw all these people, I said, man, and everybody's hollering, "Cootie, Cootie." So Cootie come up. He was home, boy. So Duke came out, Duke put on a robe and came to the platform, hollered at us. I ain't never budged. So we played Mobile that night, packed, four, five thousand people. The white was spectators. You know, down there if the colored had the dance, the white people could come as spectators. But, you know, not dance. They were spectators.
So man, Duke or somebody say he liked watermelon.

Man, we came out of the dance and got two big ones, about this big, cooling in the ice, you know. Man, we sit out there and had a field day. Had a field day. All those things. But you know, the people -- it was so wonderful. Wonderful.
